text:
The best thing about the Sharks right now is three kids on one line. Ivar Stenberg, Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith led a 4-2 win that ended Nashville's seven-game streak, a game San Jose Hockey Now headlined "Kids Are Alright." Smith's assist on a Stenberg goal got its own story at NBC Sports Bay Area. The version of the top line we track most, Smith and Celebrini with Igor Chernyshov, takes 62% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), which is the best of any regular unit here.

The rest of the team is the worry. San Jose is 10-12-2 and gets 44% of the expected goals, 45% at five on five, with a penalty kill that allows 0.96 expected goals a game. Both top defense pairs, Darnell Nurse with Michael Kesselring and Jacob Trouba with Sam Dickinson, sit near 42%, and the Nurse pair has been on for 13 goals against and 6 for. The Sharks have scored almost 11 fewer goals than their chances earned and allowed nine more than their chances against.

Yaroslav Askarov's hot start drew a Mercury News piece on whether he can sustain it, and Kiefer Sherwood is in a sling, per San Jose Hockey Now. Our playoff odds are 7%. Ryan Warsofsky's season is about the kids. On that front, it's going well.
